summary.text: Frederick Haynes is the Democratic nominee for the open Texas 30th District seat. Since 1983 he has been senior pastor of Friendship-West Baptist Church in Dallas, and he briefly led the Rainbow PUSH Coalition in 2023. He won the March 2026 Democratic primary and frames his campaign around justice, opportunity and accountability.

paragraphs.text: Born in Dallas in 1960 as Frederick Douglass Haynes III.
According to his campaign website, he has earned degrees from Bishop College, Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary, the Graduate Theological Foundation, and Christian Theological Seminary.
Became senior pastor of Friendship-West Baptist Church in Dallas in 1983; his campaign website says he grew the congregation from fewer than 100 members to more than 13,000.

According to his campaign website, he founded the THRIVE Intern and Leadership Program, which provides paid employment and job training for young people, and Friendship-West has invested more than $3 million in historically Black colleges and universities and students.
Succeeded the Rev. Jesse Jackson as chief executive officer of the Rainbow PUSH Coalition in 2023 and stepped down about three months later.

Serves in leadership roles with the Samuel DeWitt Proctor Conference, the Conference of National Black Churches, the National Action Network and the IC3 Church Conference, and is on the board of trustees of Paul Quinn College, according to his campaign website.
Took a medical leave from the pulpit in September 2025 for surgery and returned the following month.
Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 72.6% of the vote over Barbara Mallory Caraway and Rodney LaBruce.
Is running for the seat Jasmine Crockett is leaving to run for the U.S. Senate.
